chapter: Trent's band: Texas, St. Louis and the road east
title: Brown Hotel in Louisville and Lexington in 1927-28 (second version)
summary: A few nights at the Brown Hotel and a few months in a Lexington spot; the song was published there in 1928.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Had you played the Brown Hotel in Louisville?
We played the Brown Hotel in Louisville; right.
Was that a steady job or was that just one night?
We played there about three or four nights. I remember it was at the end of a street, you walked in, it was like a dead end, you walked right into the hotel. I know the Brown Hotel. That was 1928.
That's about the time Stuff played?
Yes.
Stuff was on the boat with you too?
Stuff was on the boat. 1927 we were on the boat, because this number was published in Lexington, Kentucky. We were playing in Lexington.
What, in a hotel there?
No, but it was a fine spot there. We stayed there for about two, three months.
Really? In Lexington?
In Lexington.
It doesn't seem like there would be that much business there.
Yes, there was. It was right downtown; it was a fine place.
I was talking to a guy about a month ago from Lexington, and said, the only thing wrong with the band, we couldn't go in there and play.
Oh, yeah, he was playing just for whites?
Yeah.
Was there some guy here who was from Lexington?
Who lives here now; yeah.
See if you can remember
Yeah, he would remember the place. I could call him up.
Yeah, call him up and find out.
He was a great friend of Al Bernie (phonetic spelling). I met him up at Al Bernie's party from ADC and I'll get the name. He told me the name of the place but I forgot it.
Now that's '28--yeah, this is '28.
This is '28.
Leo Mosley--do you have copies of that?
No.
1800 Rock Street, Little Rock.
That's my own spot.
